name: Residential sale and purchase — refused duplicate of Legal conveyancing and Finance household property
one_line: REFUSED: a residential sale or purchase pack is a conveyancing legal matter while active and a household acquisition or disposal record in the owner's corpus. Property is the subject, buyer and seller are party roles, and transaction stage is a document-function value; none creates a distinct construction_property template with its own detection, dimensions, or privacy rules. Absorbs the legacy label prop.sale-purchase without preserving its mistaken node.
refuse_reason: Reverses the gist draft after the required cross-family comparison. The node test fails on all three legs. (1) DETECTION: a memorandum of sale, title-and-search bundle, property questionnaires, enquiries, contract, transfer, completion statement, registration confirmation, identity checks and source-of-funds evidence are the documents and stages of conveyancing. They distinguish a conveyancing matter from generic Legal, but do not distinguish a construction_property situation from Legal's matter-file and personal-legal-matters coverage. The surviving owner-side title, closing, tax, insurance and acquisition or disposal records are already held by finance.household-property. Property addresses, buyer/seller labels and stage words are never-alone roles or values. (2) DIMENSIONS: property -> transaction -> stage merely combines the construction_property default property/site -> instruction -> document function with a legal matter lifecycle. The transaction is the legal matter or accepted group; buyer/seller is a party role; stage is a work_type or record_type value. The field-less schema supplies no legal dimension, and no distinct order remains after the Legal and Finance split. (3) PRIVACY: passports, bank statements, source-of-funds material, mortgage offers and client-account references require protection, but Legal and Finance are already safety domains and impose the same or stronger protection-first rule. Aggregation makes the pack sensitive, but does not create a construction_property privacy rule. Keeping this row would classify the same bytes by a property topic and party position, repeating the industry-label mistake the node test forbids.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every entry below is a DETECTION signal, never an extraction licence - this template's schema declares no field rows (PR-6; D1's deferral stands). “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

a transaction-stage structure: documents naming a stage on their face - offer accepted, memorandum of sale, draft contract, enquiries raised, exchange, completion - together with a property address and two identified sides. Stage vocabulary tied to one address is the discriminating shape, because it only exists while the transaction is running.

a title-and-search bundle: register entries with a title number, a title plan, and search results addressed to the property (local authority, drainage and water, environmental) - machine-generated documents with reference numbers and issue dates that no household ever produces for itself.

a standard property questionnaire: a numbered form about boundaries, disputes, alterations, services and fixtures, completed by the seller. A form whose questions are about the property rather than about a person is distinctive.

a completion or financial statement: a reconciliation of price, deposit, mortgage advance, fees, taxes and apportionments arriving at a balance due on a stated date. “Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs.”
an identity and source-of-funds pack: identity documents, address evidence and bank statements collected for anti-money-laundering purposes and filed inside the transaction, not for their own sake.
a memorandum or contract pair: two copies of the same contract signed by different parties, exchanged on a date, followed by a transfer instrument.

a purpose-coherent bundle whose members are individually unremarkable - a survey, a form, three searches, a certificate and an identity scan. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: any model step runs after P7 and under the user's policy, and must abstain rather than guess: “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”

which side the file belongs to. A buyer's file and a seller's file contain many of the same documents, and the pack is assembled by solicitors who send copies both ways. “Topic answers what a file is about, while purpose answers what the file was for.”
separating a live transaction from a completed one, when the same documents sit in both and only the presence of a completion statement or a registration confirmation says which.
separating a transaction that COLLAPSED from one that completed - an abandoned pack looks identical to a live one and is the common case nobody files deliberately.
deciding which members of a completed pack become permanent property records and which are dead paper, which is the row's central judgement and the seam with finance.household-property.
recognising a solicitor's report on title, which is prose about the whole bundle, as the document that explains the rest of the file.
never_alone: a property address alone. Every document in the pack carries one, and so does every other row in this family and every household bill - it identifies the subject and says nothing about the situation. Read across by inference from “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.”
a person's name alone: buyer, seller, solicitor, lender and agent all appear.
a title number alone - it is a permanent identifier of the land, not of any transaction over it, and it appears on records made decades apart.
a money total or a price alone.
the word contract, transfer or completion alone - all three are the most generic document words in the corpus.
a bare 4-digit number, as likely a search reference, a title fragment or a postcode fragment as a year.

membership in a download session that pulled a whole conveyancing portal folder at once - “A session should never be treated as proof of topic, and it should not carry the same confidence as a hash match or a directly extracted document fact.”

an extension or a source_type alone - “The engine should treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning, inspect the real MIME type or file signature where possible, and dispatch each file to a type-specific extractor.”

work_types: official copy of the register and title plan
survey or valuation obtained for the transaction
mortgage offer supplied into the transaction
tax return and payment confirmation for the transaction
grouping_reasons: one transaction: the whole pack, held together by a property, two sides and a period rather than by content. This is the clearest purpose-coherent group in the property family and the reason the row exists.
one document across its drafts - the contract as drafted, amended, approved and executed - which is a version family before it is anything else.
one enquiry thread: the questions raised and the replies given, which only make sense as a pair.

the pack and the mortgage that funded it, which are two situations on one transaction and should be joinable without either absorbing the other. “The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files.”
no group at all is a valid outcome: a lone official copy of the register downloaded years later is a standalone record.

template.why: Empty because the row is refused, and empty independently because construction_property declares no fields. The apparent property -> transaction -> stage order is not a distinct construction/property recommendation: property is the subject of the Legal matter and household record, transaction is the matter or accepted group, and stage is document function. Legal protection and Finance household-property coverage already organize the same lifecycle without a duplicate template.

falls_through_to.why: The first residual for this row, unusually, and the correct one for its identity, source-of-funds, bank-statement and completion-statement members with no accepted group. “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”

The home for a standalone register copy, search result or form with a durable purpose but no accepted transaction group. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

The cautious outcome for a pack whose transaction may have collapsed, or an enquiry thread whose status is unresolved. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

The safe outcome for a password-protected conveyancing portal export, which is how these packs routinely arrive. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

The home for isolated transactional members - a search fee receipt, a tax payment confirmation - that this row should not absorb into a group. “Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.”

sensitivity_why: A conveyancing pack is one of the most concentrated collections of protected material a private person ever assembles: identity documents, months of bank statements, a source-of-funds declaration, a mortgage offer stating what a household can borrow, and a completion statement with client account references - all gathered in one place because a duty required it. 00 names the corpus this product handles - it “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records.” - and identity documents and account statements head that list. The design is explicit about the moment protection begins: “A scanned passport, tax statement, medical document, authentication key, or account record should enter a protected state immediately.” The operative limits are 00's: “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.” This row assigns only the catalogue value potentially_sensitive; it does not assign, alias, rank, or infer a P7 handling class.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH NJ-CP-SP-1: confirm retirement of the legacy label rather than re-roster it under Legal. A distinct legal.conveyancing template would be justified only if its stage signals or protected view differ from legal.practice-matter-file and legal.personal-legal-matters; moving the same row across schemas without that test would preserve the duplication. NJ-CP-SP-2: decide whether buyer-side and seller-side transaction views are user-approved group views or stored role facts. This refusal treats buyer and seller as roles/values and the transaction as a reviewable group; it does not mint keys. NJ-CP-SP-3: decide which completed conveyancing records a household should retain and whether an accepted group dissolves after completion. That is a retention and user-organization decision, not evidence for a construction_property node.
